docs.title: What you will be able to do
docs.text: By the end of this training you can scale a Kubernetes deployment and prove that every replica is running.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text: Engineers who are new to Kubernetes and know how to use a terminal.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: Every step runs in your own environment: a Kubernetes cluster built for you when you press Start. Each step tells you what to do, lets you do it in the terminal, and then checks it. If you get stuck, the trainer can show or run the step's solution.

docs.title: 1. Check the Environment
docs.text: Your environment was built when you pressed Start: a Kubernetes cluster with a small demo application, the AI Travel Advisor (nginx, the Python app, Ollama, Weaviate and an OpenTelemetry Collector). Before changing anything, confirm both are up.

docs.title: 2. Scale the Web Tier
docs.text:
One replica of an application is one failure away from an outage. Kubernetes keeps as many copies of a pod running as the deployment asks for, so scaling out is a single command.

Scale the nginx web tier of the AI Travel Advisor to two replicas. Only nginx is stateless: the Python app must stay at one replica because its embedding-model override is per process.

kubectl scale deployment travel-advisor-nginx -n ai-travel-advisor --replicas=2

Then watch the second pod start:

kubectl get pods -n ai-travel-advisor -l app=travel-advisor-nginx

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
You need:

  • A Dynatrace tenant with the Enablement app installed.
  • Optional: an Arize AX account (space ID and API key). Without them the AI Travel Advisor still runs, but traces are only exported to Dynatrace. Provide them as the ARIZE_SPACE_ID and ARIZE_API_KEY secrets (Codespaces) or in .devcontainer/.env (local).
  • Nothing on your laptop: the terminal, the cluster and the AI Travel Advisor run in your environment.
